name: Tavy

attributes.attribute: fought the giant Torridge over the maiden Tamara
may have given a name to the sea spirit Davy Jones

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tavy is a Cornish folkloric figure. He is a river spirit. He fought a giant named Torridge. They fought over the maiden Tamara. Tavy won her. All three then turned into rivers. Only the Tavy joins the Tamar. The Torridge flows to a different place. Some think the name Tavy gave rise to the sea spirit Davy Jones.

okr.objective: Describe the Cornish river spirit Tavy.
key_results: Tavy fought the giant Torridge over the hand of the maiden Tamara.
The three rivals turned into rivers, and only the Tavy joins the Tamar.
The name Tavy may be the origin of Davy Jones.
